stage1.impression: A strong, graphic night image: the red wash rising in a V up board-formed concrete is a real idea, and the concrete texture holds up close. But the speaker reads as a glowing lightbox more than a crafted object, with a pink-white interior near clipping and a murky dark horn. The foot of the set falls into a crushed black band, and the puddles on the paving are soft, blobby CG shapes that give the render away.

blocking_9: The ground band where the wall meets the paving [0,1150,1600,1230] must hold detail (median luminance at least 8, crush under 10%), so the plinth and the wall's foot read as real surfaces
The wet paving must read as real wet granite: fine, irregular sheen and small puddles, not large smooth blobs with soft decal edges
The lined interior must keep its Ember colour: no near-white pink hot spots at the ports (p95 under 235)
The plinth must read as a black object with a lit lens top, not vanish into the dark
The air must carry a trace of the light (subtle haze in the wash) so the V wash reads as photographed light, not a projected decal

defects.what: Crushed black band at the wall's foot and ground (median 3.7, 29.7% crushed); the set loses its floor plane here
The plinth disappears: 13.9% crushed, only its thin glowing lens strip reads
Puddles are large smooth blobs with soft, decal-like edges; reflection inside is cut by their outlines into fragments
Port area and lower lining near clipping (p95 242, clip 0.87%), colour washing to pink-white (g 142 against r 246)
The horn reads as a murky dark-red panel with a black blob (median 15.8), the throat silhouette dominating
Vertical panel joint near the left edge (step -17) reads as a frame line
Matching vertical panel joint near the right edge (step 15), boxing the frame in symmetrically
The lower wall outside the V is almost black (median 7.4), with no moonlight modelling of the concrete
The V wash has fairly crisp diagonal edges and no air in it, so it reads a little like a projected graphic

changes.problem: The ground plane and the wall's foot are crushed to black, so the speaker floats on nothing and the plinth vanishes.

evidence.measured: lum_median 3.7, crush_pct 29.7; the plinth region [650,1145,950,1200] crush 13.9%

change.to: 0.45 (keep #C4D0F0; move position to [4.0, -6.0, 6.0] so it rakes the paving and the plinth's front face)

changes.expected: A faint cool modelling of the paving joints, the plinth's black faces and the wall's foot; still a night picture (the frame's median stays under 25).

changes.problem: The puddles are big smooth blobs with soft outlines that read as CG and chop the reflection into fragments.

evidence.measured: seen: puddle outlines are rounded blobs 200-500 px across with uniform mirror interiors

change.setting: set.props.2 (paving) puddle_m and wet; set.props.3 wet
change.to: puddle_m 0.3, wet 0.55; props.3 wet 0.7; add concrete.water-style ripple 0.02 on the puddle surfaces if the kit allows

changes.expected: A finer, broken wet sheen with smaller pooled patches in the tile joints; the speaker's reflection reads as a soft streak on wet stone rather than cut-out mirror fragments.

changes.problem: The uplight drives the lower lining and ports to near-white, washing the Ember colour to pink inside the cabinet.

change.to: 185 (and color #FFFFFF to #FFF1E0, a slightly warmer 4500 K, which suits all eight colours)

changes.expected: The ports and lining hold colour; the wall wash drops only slightly and stays the subject.

changes.problem: With c3 the wall wash must not lose its strength; the colour on the wall is half the subject.

change.to: 1.05 if the wall falls below the accept after c3 (otherwise leave)

changes.expected: The wash on the wall keeps a median near 55-65 on both sides of the speaker.

changes.problem: The light hangs in no air, so the V wash reads a little like a projection laid on the wall.

evidence.measured: lum_median 7.4 just outside the wash, a hard drop at the V's edge

changes.expected: A faint glow of red air around the speaker and softer edges to the V, with blacks lifted only slightly.

changes.problem: The plinth's top reads only as a hairline of glow and its body vanishes, so the speaker's stand has no presence.

evidence.measured: lum_median 4.5, p95 205: a thin hot line over black

change.to: 0.2, so it catches a crisp cool edge highlight from the moved moon of c1

changes.expected: A readable black block with a defined top edge under the speaker.

changes.problem: Two vertical panel joints near the frame edges box the image in like a set's flats.

evidence.measured: edge step -16.9 at x~82; right joint step 15.4 at x~1537

change.setting: set.props.7-23 (front wall panels) size w and positions
change.to: w 4.796, spaced 4.8 with one centred at 0 (joints at +/-2.4 m, outside the frame)

changes.expected: One continuous board-formed wall across the frame with no vertical lines at the edges.

out_of_scope.request: Let more light reach the horn so it reads as glowing tinted resin rather than a dark panel with a black throat silhouette
out_of_scope.why: The horn sits above the cabinet and the batts stop the uplight; brightening it would mean a second light or a change to the product, both fixed

out_of_scope.request: Make the woofer ring and cabinet's upper band read as more than dark shapes
out_of_scope.why: That is what this cabinet does with one light under it; only the product or the light placement could change it
